candidate.answerReason: The inequality is equivalent to \(\sqrt n+\sqrt{n-1}>100\). Every positive integer at most 2500 fails, while 2501 satisfies it.

methods.label: Use a conjugate and exact bounds
methods.explanation:
A difference of nearby square roots is easier to compare after multiplying by its conjugate. For a positive integer \(n\), both roots are defined and their sum is positive, so
\[
\sqrt n-\sqrt{n-1}
=\frac{n-(n-1)}{\sqrt n+\sqrt{n-1}}
=\frac1{\sqrt n+\sqrt{n-1}}.
\]
Consequently, the required strict inequality is equivalent to
\[
\sqrt n+\sqrt{n-1}>100.
\]
If \(n\le2500\), then \(\sqrt n\le50\) and \(\sqrt{n-1}<50\). Their sum is less than 100, so every such positive integer fails.

For \(n=2501\), the sum is
\[
\sqrt{2501}+\sqrt{2500}=\sqrt{2501}+50>100.
\]
Thus the smallest possible integer is \(2501\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
methods.levelReason: Exact square-root comparisons and the difference-of-squares identity suffice; no calculus or approximation is needed.

review.mathematicalCheck: The positive conjugate sum gives √n−√(n−1)=1/(√n+√(n−1)), so the required sum must exceed 100. Every positive integer n≤2500 gives a sum below 100, whereas n=2501 gives √2501+50>100. This proves both feasibility and minimality.
